bug_semantics: The unified FastAPI server supplied two publicly known, >=32-character defaults for KEYSERVER_TOKEN_SECRET and TELEMETRY_TOKEN_SECRET. validate_config() checked only length and cross-module inequality, so an operator who did not override the environment variables started the production server with those known HS256 signing keys. TokenAuth.verify_token() accepted a JWT when its signature and module issuer matched and returned the attacker-chosen sub/client_id without requiring that client to exist, allowing source-aware attackers to mint bearer tokens that passed the keyserver or telemetry route dependencies.
flaw_origin: Commit 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 created the entire openssl_encrypt_server tree and, in the same atomic commit, added both hardcoded JWT defaults, the insufficient length-only startup validation, the HS256 encode/decode path, and the authenticated route wiring. This is the first writing of the vulnerable mechanism, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or merge.
ai_marker: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com> (the same BIC commit object also says: 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code))
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-qc6h-gfjh-7qqg identifies the two config.py defaults, explains that their >=32-character values pass validation and permit JWT forgery, and names 6090a8e as the resolution. Reproduce the origin with `git log --all --reverse --format='%H %P %ad %s' --date=iso-strict -S'keyserver-secret-change-me-min-32-chars' -- openssl_encrypt_server/config.py`, which begins at 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4; repository-wide `-S` gives the same first origin. `git log 6090a8e329230b5c4b941dcedee4cc4b78bb35a7 --format='%H %P %s' -L 164,180:openssl_encrypt_server/config.py` traces the unchanged default back through formatting/CORS edits to the /dev/null addition in 8170b3e0. `git cat-file -p 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4` shows exactly one parent, 849da61d5e88aa901c6a8ec70859019a57156363, and the quoted Claude markers; `git cat-file -e 849da61d5e88aa901c6a8ec70859019a57156363:openssl_encrypt_server/config.py` fails because the path does not exist, directly proving parent absence. `git show 8170b3e0:openssl_encrypt_server/config.py` shows both known defaults and validation that only rejects lengths below 32 or equal module secrets. `git show 8170b3e0:openssl_encrypt_server/core/auth/token.py` shows HS256 jwt.encode/jwt.decode with the configured secret and issuer and returns the sub claim; the two routes.py blobs show that result guards keyserver upload/revoke and telemetry event submission. `git show 6090a8e329230b5c4b941dcedee4cc4b78bb35a7 -- openssl_encrypt_server/config.py` adds production-mode rejection of change-me/changeme-style values, closing the deploy-with-known-default path, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 6090a8e329230b5c4b941dcedee4cc4b78bb35a7` exits 0. Version history corrects the advisory metadata boundary: `git tag --contains` shows both BIC and 6090a8e first contained by v1.4.0, while `git cat-file -e v1.3.6:openssl_encrypt_server/config.py` fails; therefore the vulnerable unified-server code existed on development history between those commits but no tagged release contains the BIC without the fix. The first-party page's affected '< 1.4.0'/patched 'None' metadata is inconsistent with its own resolution and repository trees. Later defense-in-depth commit 8d0d91896ee19ea9c31951b39d72a364b594fd71 removes the defaults entirely and is first contained by v1.4.1, but it is not the advisory's direct closing fix.
reasoning: The defect is causal code written in 8170b3e0: publicly known signing material was deliberately made long enough to satisfy the simultaneously introduced validator, and that material fed directly into the JWT authentication boundary. Its immediate parent lacks the whole unified-server path, and both -S and -L independently identify this one-parent creation commit, so later formatting and security commits are not introducers. The BIC commit object itself explicitly says it was generated with Claude Code and carries a Claude Sonnet 4.5 Co-Authored-By trailer; under the BIC-only rule this is direct AI authorship evidence on the root-cause change. Commit 6090a8e is the first direct production startup rejection of the known defaults and is explicitly named by the first-party advisory, so the lifecycle is closed even though later 8d0d9189 further hardens debug/development behavior by eliminating defaults.
